title: Electronic submission of OSHA injury and illness records: burden appears small

history.reason: OSHA's own estimate is about $136 per year per affected establishment, and only establishments with 100+ employees are covered; evidence argues against pursuing this as a startup problem.

description: Establishments with 100 or more employees in designated industries must submit injury and illness records electronically each year; OSHA estimates the added cost is small.
customer_segment: Establishments with 100+ employees in OSHA-designated industries (not small businesses by employee count).
context: Rule published July 2023. Reopen only with independent evidence that the cost or error burden is materially larger than OSHA estimates.

evidence.text: OSHA estimates an average cost of $136 per year for affected establishments (annualized over 10 years at 7%).
Only establishments with 100 or more employees in designated industries are required to submit Forms 300 and 301 electronically.
OSHA states the information submitted is already required to be kept.

alternatives: Manual entry through OSHA's submission portal; existing safety-management software: not investigated.

contradictory_evidence.text: The only quantified burden is OSHA's own estimate, which is very low; independent evidence of higher cost was not found.

uncertainty: Unknown: actual time spent, error or penalty exposure, and whether recordkeeping itself (as opposed to electronic submission) is burdensome.
open_questions: Is the underlying injury recordkeeping process, rather than submission, the pain point?
next_actions: Reopen only with independent evidence of material cost.
